descricao_original: The trachea and initial portions of the primary bronchi are extrapulmonary conducting passageways. After passing into the lung, the primary bronchi, their branches and continuing bronchioles constitute the intrapulmonary conducting passageways. These passageways serve to convey air, no gas exchange occurs. Bronchioles lead into respiratory passageways that are distinguished by the presence of alveoli in their walls where gas exchange occurs. Respiratory passageways are all intrapulmonary.
